Two identical closed glass jars side by side. The left jar is: inside, there is no liquid at the bottom, just a few scattered blue circles with arrows showing them bouncing around as vapour molecules. The right jar is: it has a pool of blue liquid at the bottom, many more vapour molecules crowded in the space above, and double-headed arrows indicating molecules simultaneously leaving the liquid (evaporating) and entering the liquid (condensing). Three mercury barometer tubes inverted into a trough of mercury. Tube 1 shows a normal mercury column of height H (e.g., 760 mm) with an empty vacuum space above. Tube 2 shows a few drops of liquid introduced; the mercury column has dropped slightly, and the space above contains invisible vapour. Tube 3 shows more liquid added; the mercury column has dropped further to a lower height h, and a thin visible layer of liquid floats on top of the mercury. Clean flat textbook illustration, white background.

A wet and dry bulb hygrometer mounted on a wooden board. Two glass thermometers are placed side by side. The left thermometer (Dry Bulb) has a completely exposed bulb and shows a higher red column reading. The right thermometer (Wet Bulb) has its bulb wrapped tightly in a piece of white muslin cloth that extends downward into a small glass reservoir of water at the bottom. The reading on the wet bulb is noticeably lower. Clean flat textbook illustration, white background.
